notes: Corrected: the italic of an ephah is split off as its own added unit. It supplies a preposition, an article and a measure noun in a clause whose Hebrew names none of them, which is exactly rule 33's added case and the reeds precedent; the accepted alignment folded it into עֶשְׂרֹנִים under rule 31 while itself calling it a supplied measure.
עֶשְׂרֹנִים keeps the supplied generic parts and heads on tenth under rule 31; only the measure phrase moved.
fine flour is headed on flour under rule 31's tie clause, with the competing reading recorded in that unit's note.
The supplied in of in one cake is placed under rule 33 on the word it stands before in the English; putting it on חַלָּה is the defensible alternative and is named in that unit's note.
